title: policy.json: merge
description: The basic local merge queue (design part 14): main is fast-forwarded only to a commit that passed the full suite as part of its batch.

mode.description: Who decides each merge. "queue": the orchestrator runs the queue whenever branches are waiting. "owner": the queue first rebases each finished branch and runs the fast checks, the scanners and the full suite without moving main (hitld merge); a branch that fails goes back to its executor, and only green branches are presented to the owner, with evidence, in one question for the batch. The owner approves all (hitld merge --all) or a list (hitld merge --only <branch>). A new project starts in owner mode; the queue is opted into once the record supports it.

via.description: How main moves. "push": the queue fast-forwards main to the tested commit locally. "pull-request": for a session that cannot push main (a cloud session, a protected main), the queue opens or updates a GitHub pull request for each waiting branch, waits for the checks merge.pull_request.checks names, and squash-merges it through the GitHub API with the item's trailers and, in owner mode, the owner's Signed-off-by from the recorded approval; after each merge the next branch is brought up to date with main (merged, never force-pushed), rebuilt and checked again. GitHub is reached through the GitHub command line's own sign-in; HITLd stores no token.

pull_request.description: With merge.via pull-request: which checks gate a pull request, how long one may run, the owner's decision that delegated merging without asking, and the remote that is GitHub.

checks.description: The checks a pull request waits for, by check-run name or status context; others are not waited for. With none, the queue merges nothing.

check_timeout_minutes.description: How long a named check may stay unfinished on a pull request's head before the queue goes on without it; the pull request is reported as stalled and stays waiting.

conditional_checks.description: Checks a pull request also waits for unless every file it changes matches the check's unless_only globs: for a check CI reports only for some changes, such as the code scanning result for code CodeQL analyzes, which a text-only pull request never gets. An empty change waits for each.

name.description: The check-run name or status context.

unless_only.description: The files whose change alone does not call for the check.

delegated_by.description: In owner mode, the owner's decision that delegated merging, without asking, the pull requests that change nothing under merge.owner_paths or in merge.owner_areas. With it, such a pull request's squash commit carries the owner's Signed-off-by (the one their latest approval gave) and a Delegated-by trailer naming this decision; with no sign-off of theirs known yet, it waits for the owner. Without it, such a pull request merges with no sign-off, as in queue mode.

remote.description: The git remote that is the GitHub repository; its URL names the repository.

owner_paths.description: In owner mode, limits what waits for the owner: a branch that changes a file under these globs waits; a branch that changes nothing here or in owner_areas goes through the queue as in queue mode (with merge.via pull-request, it is merged once its named checks pass). The globs are read in order and the last one a file matches decides; one that starts with "!" takes the files it matches back out, so ["**", "!work/**"] holds everything but the tracker. A file no glob matches does not wait. With this and owner_areas both empty, every branch waits.

owner_areas.description: In owner mode, limits what waits for the owner by area (policy rights.areas): a branch that changes a file in one of these areas waits. "unassigned" names the files in no area. With this and owner_paths both empty, every branch waits.

public_globs.description: The project's public surface (design 6.6): APIs, formats, names others rely on. In owner mode, a presented branch that changes a file here carries a directed read of the public signatures and docs, and for a JSON schema, the fields added, removed or changed.

propose_queue_after.description: In owner mode, how many merges in a row in one area, each approved as presented and none reverted, before hitld merge proposes letting the queue merge that area without asking. The proposal is a question for the owner; the system never changes merge.mode or the owner settings itself.

main_branch.description: The integration branch: the one main-branch setting (HITLD-82). Only the merge queue moves it; the orchestrator creates items and gives up claims on it, and claims are read from every other branch.

batch_max.description: The most branches in one batch before the full suite runs. Smaller batches make bisection cheaper.

fast_checks.description: Commands run on each rebased branch before it joins the batch: lint, type check, the item's acceptance checks, the tests nearest its touches. Each runs through the shell in the queue's worktree with HITLD_ITEM, HITLD_TOUCHES and HITLD_CHANGED_FILES set. A failure sends the branch back to its executor.
fast_checks.x-hitld-executes: each entry is run through the shell in the merge queue's worktree

scanners.description: Security scanners, run on each rebased branch after the fast checks (design 10.5 and 14.2): static analysis and dependency audits. None is built in. Each runs through the shell in the queue's worktree and writes its findings in its output format to the file named by $HITLD_SARIF, or to its standard output; its exit status is ignored, and output that is not SARIF fails the branch. A finding in neither the baseline nor the recorded verdicts in the private store sends the branch back with the finding. The first scan, and a new tool or rule version's first run, scans main and makes or extends the baseline instead of failing.

command.description: The command that scans the current directory, which is the branch under test. $HITLD_PRIMARY_ROOT is the primary checkout the policy was read from: a script kept in the repository is run from there (node "$HITLD_PRIMARY_ROOT/scripts/scan.mjs"), never by a relative path, which would run the branch's own copy.
command.x-hitld-executes: run through the shell in the merge queue's worktree

format.description: The output format. SARIF is the only one read.

scanners.x-hitld-executes: each entry's command is run through the shell in the merge queue's worktree

full_suite.description: The full test suite, run once per batch on the combined result. With none, the queue refuses to move main, because it could not keep main green.
full_suite.x-hitld-executes: each entry is run through the shell in the merge queue's worktree

generated.description: Generated files: never merged by hand. A rebase conflict confined to them takes the batch's version, and the regenerate command rebuilds them once per batch, before the full suite.

regenerate.description: The command that rebuilds them, run through the shell at the batch's root.
regenerate.x-hitld-executes: run through the shell in the merge queue's worktree

flake_reruns.description: How many times a failing full suite is rerun on the same commit. A pass on a rerun makes the failure a flake candidate, and the comparison on the batch's base decides whether the batch is blamed (design 14.4 and 14.7; policy flake). With 0, a failure is not rerun and the batch is bisected at once.

require_private_list.description: Whether hitld merge refuses (private-list-invalid) when the private term list is not there to check every commit against, as in a session that has not pulled the private store. Off by default: the merge then checks the terms implied here (the store address in use, device names) and warns that the list was not checked, so a cloud session with the store address and no device key keeps merging. Turn it on where the store is always pulled before a merge.
